environmentalPersistence: Moderate — K⁺ is moderately mobile in soil; leaches less than nitrate but more than phosphate

lowDose.description: Optimal — improved turgor pressure, enhanced stomatal regulation, stronger stems, better drought resistance, improved fruit quality. Plants appear vigorous with good structural integrity.

highDose.description: Potassium toxicity — induces magnesium and calcium deficiency, causes leaf margin scorch/necrosis, disrupts osmotic balance, reduces Mg-dependent enzyme activity including chlorophyll synthesis.

morphologicalEffects.heightSuppression: Negative at low dose (promotes sturdy growth); moderate at high dose via Mg/Ca antagonism
morphologicalEffects.leafSize: Increased at low dose; scorch-marginned at high dose
morphologicalEffects.wilting: Reduced at low dose (better turgor); mild at high dose from Mg deficiency
morphologicalEffects.chlorosis: Absent at low dose; interveinal chlorosis at high dose (Mg deficiency — Mg needed for chlorophyll)
morphologicalEffects.necrosis: Leaf margin scorch at high dose — classic K toxicity pattern
morphologicalEffects.rootGrowth: Stimulated at low dose; mildly inhibited at high dose
morphologicalEffects.newVsOldLeaves: K deficiency (opposite scenario) affects old leaves first; excess K toxicity appears on margins of all leaves

physiologyEffects.chlorophyllReduction: Absent at low dose; moderate at high dose via Mg antagonism
physiologyEffects.photosyntheticRate: Increased at low dose; reduced at high dose
physiologyEffects.stomatalConductance: Strongly improved at low dose (K is the key stomatal motor ion); mildly reduced at high dose
physiologyEffects.transpiration: Optimized at low dose; disrupted at high dose
physiologyEffects.waterUptake: Enhanced at low dose; mildly impaired at high dose

molecularEffects.oxidativeStress: Only at high dose via Mg/Ca deficiency

microbiomeEffects.diversityReduction: Minimal at optimal; mild at high dose
microbiomeEffects.rhizosphereStability: Stable at optimal; mildly disrupted at high dose

temporalDynamics.firstSymptomsHours: 96–168 hours for toxicity; 48–96 hours for beneficial effects
firstSymptoms: leaf margin yellowing at high dose

visualSimulation.colorChanges: Low dose: vigorous green, upright. High dose: margin scorch (brown edges), interveinal chlorosis
visualSimulation.firstAffectedRegion: Leaf margins at high dose; whole-plant vigor improvement at low dose
visualSimulation.damagePattern: Margin scorch — distinguishes K toxicity from N toxicity (tip) and P toxicity (interveinal on young leaves)
visualSimulation.heatmapGlow: Moderate — malate/stomatal signature at low dose; Mg-deficiency marker at high dose
visualSimulation.recoveryVisual: Moderate — margin scorch remains; new growth healthy

synergies.synergyNote: K completes the NPK trio — K is the structural and physiological regulator while N builds mass and P builds roots/energy. K also buffers against drought and disease stress.
synergies.antagonismNote: High salt (NaCl) competes with K⁺ at uptake sites — salt stress mimics K deficiency. High K antagonizes Mg and Ca uptake.

educationalContext.realWorldSources: Potash mining (primary sources: Canada, Russia, Belarus), wood ash, manure
educationalContext.agriculturalUse: Third most used fertilizer globally; critical for fruit and vegetable quality, disease resistance, and water use efficiency
educationalContext.humanToxicity: Low — K⁺ is essential for human health; excess in IV form can cause cardiac arrest but no risk from agricultural exposure
educationalContext.climateLink: K improves drought tolerance — increasingly relevant as climate change drives water stress in agriculture
educationalContext.indoorOutdoor: Outdoor — agricultural/horticultural; indoor in houseplant fertilizers
educationalContext.whyStudentsCare: Potassium is why bananas are healthy food — and why sports drinks replenish K after exercise. The same ion that regulates plant stomata regulates human nerve firing.
educationalContext.realWorldIssue: Sustainable potash mining, food security, drought-resilient agriculture
